主要内容: Ulta Beauty is accelerating its curbside pickup and introducing same-day delivery to cater to consumers who have grown accustomed to online shopping during the pandemic. The company's financial outlook for fiscal 2022 through 2024 anticipates diluted earnings per share growth in the low double-digits, with capital expenditures between 4% and 5% of sales, translating to $1.1 billion to $1.4 billion. Ulta expects its net sales growth to outpace the broader beauty and personal care industry, with a target of 5% to 7% versus 2% to 4% for the rest of the industry. Same-store sales are projected to rise between 3% and 5% annually, with 50 new stores opening each year. However, shares fell over 10% on Tuesday due to the company's forecast falling short of investor expectations. The pandemic has significantly impacted the high-touch beauty industry, forcing retailers like Ulta to adapt by offering more digital and contactless services. Ulta added curbside pickup in April 2020 and saw a 17.9% decline in sales online and in stores open for at least 14 months during the fiscal year ended Jan. 30. Despite these challenges, Ulta's second-quarter same-store sales rose 56.3% compared to the year-ago period, indicating a rebound in consumer demand. Ulta Beauty is adapting to evolving consumer habits by emphasizing speedy delivery and digital engagement. The company is focusing on attracting more Black and Hispanic customers through an expanded assortment of textured-hair products. Ulta executives noted that some pandemic-related behaviors, such as self-care routines and increased interest in wellness-related beauty products, are likely to persist. Chief Operating Officer Kecia Steelman highlighted the blurring line between in-person and online shopping, with customers using TikTok videos to inspire purchases and later visiting stores for in-person experiences. Chief Digital Officer Prama Bhatt emphasized that customers who shop across both channels spend significantly more and make more purchases annually. In response, Ulta plans to roll out same-day delivery in select markets ahead of the holidays, though details on fees and availability remain undisclosed. The company also aims to have curbside pickup orders ready within two hours. Competitor Sephora has already launched same-day delivery in major cities with a flat fee of $6.95.
